For deeper work, UserWay offers managed services with human experts who audit and fix content, plus tools for documents and PDFs. Reports and accessibility statements help show good faith efforts toward compliance. The product works with common platforms such as WordPress, Shopify, and Wix.

item.title: Vertex
item.description:
Vertex helps businesses get sales and use tax, VAT, and similar indirect taxes right. When a company sells a product, the right tax depends on the buyer’s location, the product type, and applicable rules, which change often. Vertex maintains a large database of rates and rules, and its engine calculates the correct tax inside systems like SAP, Oracle, and Microsoft Dynamics.

The company also covers filing and reporting. Tools prepare returns, manage exemption certificates, and support e-invoicing mandates that countries are introducing. AI features help classify products to the right tax codes and speed up compliance work. Customers are mostly large enterprises with complex tax footprints across many jurisdictions.

item.title: Wisdom Panel
item.description:
Wisdom Panel offers genetic testing for dogs and cats. An owner swabs the pet’s cheek, mails the sample, and receives a report on breed ancestry, family tree, and traits. The report also screens for genetic health conditions the pet may carry or be at risk for, which can inform decisions with a veterinarian.

The company draws on a large database of breed samples and research, and sells tests through retailers, directly to owners, and through veterinary clinics. Health screening results are meant to start conversations with a vet, and some conditions come with guidance on diet or monitoring. The brand belongs to Mars Petcare, which also owns other pet care businesses.

item.title: Aquant
item.description:
Aquant is a service intelligence platform. Equipment makers and service organizations hold years of repair history, manuals, and technician notes, which are hard to search in the moment. Aquant uses AI to learn from that data and recommend probable causes and fixes for a given symptom.

For a technician on a job, this works like an expert on call. They describe the problem or enter an error code, and the system suggests what to check, which parts are likely needed, and what has worked on similar cases. Service managers use the same data to see recurring failures and to reduce repeat visits and unnecessary parts.

item.title: Bluebeam
item.description:
Bluebeam Revu is a PDF tool built for construction. Teams review plans on screen, add markups such as clouds, callouts, and stamps, and measure lengths, areas, and counts directly on drawings to prepare quantity takeoffs for estimates. Custom tool sets store commonly used markups.

Collaboration is a big part. Studio Sessions let many people mark up the same document at the same time, and Studio Projects store drawing sets in the cloud. Overlay and comparison features show what changed between revisions, with AI helping to line up sheets and highlight differences, which reduces missed updates.

item.title: Buildertrend
item.description:
Buildertrend focuses on residential construction. Builders manage a project from estimate to completion in a single system: schedules, selections, budgets, purchase orders, daily logs, photos, and documents. Clients can log in to approve choices, view progress, and see invoices, which cuts down on phone calls.

Financial tools track costs against budgets, handle change orders, and send bills and payments. Subcontractors get access to their schedules and tasks, and mobile apps let teams update from the job site. AI features assist with tasks like summarizing communication and extracting data from documents.

item.title: Cognite
item.description:
Cognite addresses data silos in industry. A plant produces time series from sensors, maintenance records, engineering diagrams, and 3D models that live in different systems. Cognite Data Fusion links them into a graph in which a pump, its sensor readings, its work orders, and its drawings are connected, so people and applications can find everything about an asset.

That foundation supports applications. Teams build digital twins, predictive maintenance models, and dashboards, and an AI assistant helps users ask questions about assets and operations in natural language. The platform is used in oil and gas, power, and manufacturing, where downtime is costly.

item.title: Dental Monitoring
item.description:
Dental Monitoring lets orthodontists check on patients remotely. A patient attaches a small cheek retractor to a phone, scans their teeth on a schedule, and uploads the images. The software compares scans to the treatment plan and measures how teeth are moving.

AI flags problems such as aligners that do not fit, lost attachments, hygiene concerns, or progress that is behind schedule. The orthodontist reviews alerts and decides whether to adjust the plan, send the next aligners earlier, or schedule a visit. This can reduce in-person appointments and catch issues sooner.

item.title: Eyenuk
item.description:
Eyenuk focuses on automated eye screening. A technician captures retinal images with a compatible camera, and EyeArt analyzes them and reports whether signs of more-than-mild disease are present, flagging patients who need referral. The process takes about a minute and does not need a specialist to read the images.

The purpose is to expand screening for people with diabetes who miss annual eye exams. Primary care clinics, endocrinology practices, and optometrists use it to catch disease earlier. The company has expanded the technology to other conditions and offers versions for different clinical settings.

item.title: ForeFlight
item.description:
ForeFlight is an app for planning and flying. Pilots build routes, check weather and airspace, file flight plans, and view approach plates and charts. In the air, it shows moving maps and traffic and weather from compatible receivers, which replaces paper charts.

Weather is a big part. Layers show forecasts, radar, and hazards, and tools highlight conditions most likely to affect a given route. Performance and weight and balance planning help with safety, and integrations connect to avionics and tablets. Teams in flight departments use it to share data.

item.title: Greenlight Guru
item.description:
Greenlight Guru serves a heavily regulated industry. Medical device makers must document how a product was designed, how risks were assessed, and how problems are corrected. The platform organizes these records, links requirements to risks and tests, and keeps them audit ready, replacing documents scattered in shared drives.

Modules cover design controls, risk management, document control, training, supplier management, and corrective and preventive actions. AI features help draft documents and risk analyses and answer questions about regulations, saving time on repetitive writing. A clinical module supports post-market work.

item.title: Instrumentl
item.description:
Instrumentl is a grant discovery and management platform. A nonprofit describes its mission and programs, and the system recommends foundation and government grants that fit, with details on the funder’s giving history, typical award sizes, and past recipients. Alerts notify the team when new matches appear.

Once a grant is identified, a tracker handles tasks, deadlines, reports, and documents for each application, with collaboration for the team. AI assists with research, summarizing funder priorities and drafting parts of proposals, though grant writing still depends on strong program knowledge.

item.title: Mentalyc
item.description:
Mentalyc is an AI note-taking tool for mental health professionals. A therapist records a session, uploads audio, or enters brief notes, and the tool generates a structured progress note that matches the format their practice uses. The clinician edits and approves it.

The product emphasizes privacy, since therapy content is sensitive. It states that it follows health privacy rules and offers controls such as removing identifying details. It also supports treatment plans and can learn a therapist’s style over time.

item.title: Notarize (Proof)
item.description:
Notarize brought notarization online. A signer uploads a document, verifies identity by scanning an ID and answering questions, joins a video call with a commissioned notary, and signs digitally. The notary applies a digital seal and the document is stored securely, making a process that required an in-person visit possible from home.

The company, now operating as Proof, expanded into broader identity and signature products for businesses, including title and escrow, banks, and real estate. AI-based checks examine ID documents and confirm that a live person is present, which helps resist fraud.

item.title: Tracers
item.description:
Tracers is an investigative data service. A user enters a name, address, or other identifier, and the platform returns linked records about people and businesses, such as addresses, relatives, liens, and court filings. Matching algorithms connect pieces of information.

Customers include private investigators, attorneys, collections agencies, and law enforcement. Access is restricted by law in many cases and requires a permissible purpose, and results have limits in accuracy.

Tracers is sold on subscription and per search. Using such data raises privacy and legal issues, and background checks used for employment or housing are subject to consumer reporting laws. Alternatives include LexisNexis Accurint, TLOxp, Thomson Reuters CLEAR, and IRB Search. Tracers suits licensed investigative professionals.

item.title: Tractable
item.description:
Tractable applies computer vision to insurance claims. After an accident, a policyholder or repairer uploads photos, and the AI identifies damaged parts and estimates repair costs, speeding up decisions that used to wait for an inspection.

Insurers use it to settle simple claims fast, to triage complex ones, and to detect inconsistencies. The company has expanded to property damage after disasters and to the used-parts and repair industries.

Tractable is sold to insurers and repair networks on enterprise contracts. Automated estimates affect people’s payments, so fairness, accuracy, and appeal routes matter. Alternatives include CCC Intelligent Solutions, Solera, Mitchell, Shift Technology, and Cambridge Mobile Telematics. Tractable suits insurers speeding up claims.

item.title: Upheal
item.description:
Upheal helps therapists reduce paperwork. With client consent, the tool records or transcribes a session and drafts a note in the clinician’s preferred format, which they review and sign. It can summarize progress over time and suggest treatment plan updates.

The product emphasizes privacy and compliance with health data rules, and offers a free tier for solo practitioners. Session insights, such as talk time and themes, give feedback to the clinician.

item.title: Wildbook
item.description:
Wildbook turns photos into population data. Scientists and citizen scientists upload pictures of animals such as whale sharks, giraffes, and sea turtles, and the software recognizes individuals by distinctive markings, such as spot patterns or fin shapes, and links sightings over time.

That reveals movement, survival, and population size without physically tagging animals. The platform supports many species, with separate databases for each, and photos from tourists and social media can contribute.

item.title: Momentic Mo
item.description:
Mo takes an exploratory approach to testing. Instead of writing scripts for each test, a team points Mo at an app and supplies login credentials, and AI agents navigate the interface, trying flows, entering unusual inputs, and checking for errors or broken behavior. The agents report what they find.

Momentic’s wider platform helps teams write and maintain end-to-end tests in natural language, which reduces upkeep when interfaces change. Mo complements that by finding issues no one thought to test, like a human tester poking around.

item.title: NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform
item.description:
The platform responds to a security worry: autonomous agents that can run commands and access data need limits that a compromised agent cannot disable. OpenShell is an open-source runtime that places each agent in its own sandbox with policy-based permissions, and a prover checks that granted permissions cannot combine into something the operator did not intend.

Sentry adds enforcement outside the agent’s machine. It runs on BlueField data processing units, which sit apart from the host, so it can watch behavior and isolate an agent quickly even if the host is compromised. NVIDIA has described it as a reference design, with many partners integrating the pieces.

item.title: QA Wolf
item.description:
QA Wolf offers testing as a service. Instead of a company writing and maintaining its own automated tests, QA Wolf’s team creates Playwright tests for the critical flows, runs them in parallel on every release, and fixes tests when the app changes. They report real bugs, and filter flaky failures.

AI generates and repairs tests, while engineers verify results. The aim is high coverage without the burden of test maintenance, which often overwhelms small teams. Tests are written in open frameworks, so customers own the code.

item.title: Ivo
item.description:
Ivo is an AI contract review tool built for in-house legal teams. A lawyer opens an incoming contract, and Ivo compares it with the team’s preferred positions, flags issues, and suggests redlines in the document, using the editor the lawyer already works in.

Beyond review, Ivo has added tools to manage the whole flow. Business users submit requests, contracts are routed to the right reviewers, negotiations are tracked, and approvals are collected. A repository holds executed agreements for analysis.

item.title: Natural
item.description:
Natural addresses a gap in agent infrastructure: how an AI agent pays for things. Through its API, developers create an account for an agent, fund it, set spending rules, and let it pay vendors, receive money, or issue virtual cards for purchases.

Controls matter, since a spending agent can cause damage. Limits, approvals, and logs let the owner decide what an agent may buy and see what it did. The company positions this as payments infrastructure for a future where agents transact with each other and with businesses.

item.title: AI for Developers
item.description:
AI for Developers is written for people who build software and want to use AI well. Issues tend to focus on how to do things: setting up an AI coding assistant, writing prompts for common programming tasks, comparing tools, or building small projects with language model APIs. The tone is practical rather than speculative.

A developer-focused newsletter fills a gap between general AI news and academic papers. Readers look for ideas they can apply the same day, such as workflows for code review, testing, or documentation, and for honest comparisons that show what works and what does not. The Substack format also lets readers comment and share tips.

item.title: Superhuman AI
item.description:
Superhuman AI is a free daily email aimed at professionals who want to apply AI at work. Issues summarize news in brief, then spend time on practical advice: tools worth trying, prompts that work, and ways to save time.

The audience skews toward business users and non-technical readers rather than researchers. The newsletter is supported by sponsors, which are labeled, and has grown to one of the larger AI newsletters.

item.title: The Neuron
item.description:
The Neuron is a free email for people who want to follow AI without a technical background. Each issue picks a few stories, explains them in accessible language, and points to tools worth trying. The tone is conversational and avoids excessive jargon.

It includes practical sections, such as prompts and tutorials, and links to its own resources. The newsletter is supported by sponsors, which are labeled.

It is free. As with other daily newsletters, coverage is selective. Alternatives include The Rundown AI, Superhuman AI, TLDR AI, Ben’s Bites, and The Batch. The Neuron suits professionals who want a quick daily AI update.

item.title: The Rundown AI
item.description:
The Rundown AI is one of the most widely read AI newsletters. Each issue covers major stories, new tools, and research in a few minutes of reading, with a consistent format that makes it easy to skim. Sections highlight top stories, quick hits, and tools.

Beyond the newsletter, the brand offers a community, courses, and a product directory. Sponsorship supports the free edition.

The Rundown AI is free. Daily newsletters can repeat the same headlines, so readers often choose one or two. Alternatives include The Neuron, TLDR AI, Superhuman AI, Ben’s Bites, and The Batch. The Rundown AI suits people who want a fast daily briefing.

item.title: ManyChat
item.description: ManyChat lets businesses and creators respond to people in direct messages at scale. A visual flow builder defines how a conversation proceeds: someone comments a keyword on an Instagram post, ManyChat sends a DM with a link or a guide, asks questions, collects an email address, and tags the contact. It is widely used by influencers and online businesses to deliver lead magnets, run giveaways, and sell products through chat.

item.title: DroneDeploy
item.description:
DroneDeploy is a platform for drone data. Users plan an automated flight from a tablet or phone, the drone captures images, and the software stitches them into orthomosaic maps and 3D models. From these, it can measure distances, areas, and volumes, such as a stockpile or excavation.

Repeat flights show progress. Construction teams compare site conditions to plans, farmers monitor crop health, and mining operations measure material movement. AI detects objects and changes, and the platform has expanded to capture from ground robots and 360 cameras for indoor progress tracking.

item.title: Isomorphic Labs
item.description:
Isomorphic Labs aims to use AI to design medicines. It builds on DeepMind’s work on predicting protein structures and extends the idea to the interactions between proteins and drug molecules, so models can propose compounds that bind to a target. The goal is to reduce the time and cost of finding candidates.

Rather than selling software, the company runs drug discovery programs, both on its own and in collaboration with pharmaceutical companies. It has described building a platform that can be applied across diseases, with early efforts in areas such as oncology and immunology.

item.title: Overjet
item.description:
Overjet is dental AI that reads radiographs. When a dentist takes X-rays, the software outlines suspected cavities, measures bone levels, and identifies calculus and other issues, giving a second look that supports diagnosis and helps explain problems to patients by showing them the marked images.

The technology also serves payers. Insurers use it to review claims and check whether treatment matches findings, and large dental groups use it to standardize care across offices. It has regulatory clearance for several functions in the US.

item.title: PagerDuty
item.description:
PagerDuty is an incident management platform. Monitoring tools send alerts, and PagerDuty decides who should respond based on schedules and escalation rules, notifying them by phone, text, or app. It groups related alerts so one problem does not create a flood of pages.

During an incident, it supports coordination: a timeline, chat integrations, status pages, and runbooks for common fixes. AI features summarize the situation, suggest causes based on past incidents, and help write postmortems. Automation can run diagnostic or remediation steps.

item.title: Skydio
item.description:
Skydio drones fly themselves safely. Cameras and onboard computing let the drone see its surroundings and avoid obstacles in real time, even in complex places such as under bridges or around structures, which reduces crashes and operator skill demands.

Software supports missions: automated inspection routes, 3D scans of structures, and live video for first responders. Docks let drones launch and land on their own for repeated tasks. Customers include police and fire departments, utilities, infrastructure inspectors, and defense agencies.

item.title: Cellebrite
item.description:
Cellebrite is a digital forensics company. Its tools pull data from mobile devices, cloud accounts, and computers, including deleted items where possible, and organize it so investigators can review messages, photos, locations, and app activity. The company serves police, intelligence agencies, and corporate security teams.

Analysis products help investigators manage large amounts of data. AI can classify images, search through text, find connections between people and devices, and build timelines. Cloud platforms support collaboration across a case and sharing evidence with prosecutors.

item.title: Crisalix
item.description:
Crisalix builds simulation tools for aesthetic medicine. A surgeon takes photos of a patient, the software builds a 3D model of the face or body, and the surgeon adjusts parameters to show what a procedure might look like. Patients can see and discuss options before deciding.

The aim is to improve communication and set realistic expectations. A visual helps patients and surgeons align on goals, and consultations can be more productive. The company sells to plastic surgeons, dermatologists, and clinics, and has tools for marketing and patient engagement.

item.title: ESHA Genesis R&D
item.description:
Genesis R&D is a long-standing tool for food product development. A formulator enters ingredients and amounts, and the software calculates nutrients using a large food database, then generates a nutrition facts panel and an ingredient list formatted for regulatory requirements in different countries.

It also helps with design choices. Users can compare formulas, adjust ingredients to hit targets for calories, sodium, or protein, check claims such as low fat or high fiber, and flag allergens. These features reduce the risk of labeling errors, which can lead to recalls.

item.title: Givebutter
item.description:
Givebutter is a fundraising platform for nonprofits. Organizations create donation forms, run crowdfunding and peer-to-peer campaigns, sell event tickets, and accept recurring gifts. Its donor CRM keeps a record of each supporter’s giving and communications.

The platform tries to be affordable for small groups. It has been known for a model where donors can choose to tip the platform rather than the nonprofit paying fees. Auctions, text-to-give, and email tools are included. AI helps segment lists and draft appeals and thank-yous.

item.title: Holistiplan
item.description:
Holistiplan helps financial advisors use tax returns in planning. An advisor uploads a client’s return, and the software extracts the figures and generates a summary showing income, deductions, brackets, and observations. It highlights ideas worth discussing, such as Roth conversions, capital gains harvesting, or the timing of donations.

Scenarios let advisors model the effect of a strategy on taxes. Reports are designed to be shared with clients, helping advisors show value beyond investments. AI assists with reading documents and drafting talking points.

item.title: Trainerize
item.description:
Trainerize is a coaching platform for fitness professionals. Trainers create programs from an exercise library, assign them to clients, and monitor workouts logged in a mobile app. Messaging, habit tracking, and progress photos keep clients engaged.

Additional features include nutrition coaching, integrations with wearables, payment processing, and a branded app. AI helps draft programs and suggest changes based on adherence and goals.

Trainerize has a free tier for a small number of clients and paid plans. It is owned by ABC Fitness. Alternatives include TrueCoach, Everfit, PT Distinction, Mindbody, and Hevy Coach. Trainerize suits independent trainers and gyms.

item.title: EnergyCAP
item.description:
EnergyCAP collects utility bills and meter data and puts them into one system. Facility managers, energy consultants, and sustainability teams use it to track electricity, gas, water, and other utilities across a portfolio, pay bills, and report on costs and emissions.

Analytics find savings. The software flags bills with errors, such as duplicate charges or wrong rates, and highlights usage that departs from normal patterns, which may point to equipment problems. Benchmarking compares buildings, and reports support sustainability disclosures and incentive programs.

item.title: accessiBe
item.description:
accessiBe promises to make websites more accessible with minimal effort. A line of code adds an accessibility interface for visitors, with options such as larger text, contrast adjustments, and keyboard navigation, while AI runs in the background to detect issues like missing image descriptions and improper labels and attempt to fix them. Businesses use it to reduce the risk of accessibility lawsuits and to serve users with disabilities.

The company has built other products, including audits, monitoring, and expert-assisted remediation. It reports compliance status and offers statements that businesses can publish. Its marketing emphasized automation and quick compliance.

item.title: Adobe Character Animator
item.description:
Character Animator brings puppets to life. You prepare a character in Photoshop or Illustrator with layers for eyes, mouth, and body parts, import it, and the software maps your face and voice to the character. As you speak and move, the character blinks, talks, and reacts in real time, with lip sync generated from your audio.

It was designed for speed. Rigged characters can be recorded live, and the performance can be edited afterward on a timeline. Triggers set up with keyboard keys can switch poses, props, or expressions. The tool has been used for animated shows, live broadcasts, and explainer videos, and it integrates with Premiere Pro and After Effects.

item.title: Alchemy
item.description:
Alchemy gives developers a reliable way to talk to blockchains. Running your own Ethereum node takes expertise and hardware, so most teams rent access instead. Alchemy offers that through APIs that read data, send transactions, and subscribe to events, supporting Ethereum and many other networks, including layer 2 chains. Its infrastructure is built for uptime and speed, which matters when an app depends on real-time chain data.

On top of raw node access are higher-level tools. Enhanced APIs return token balances, NFT metadata, transaction history, and transfers in a form that is easier to use than raw blockchain data. Smart wallet and account abstraction tools let apps create wallets and sponsor gas fees for users, rollup services help teams launch their own chains, and webhooks and subgraphs deliver data to applications. Dashboards show request volume, errors, and latency.

item.title: Audible
item.description:
Audible made audiobooks mainstream. Members get monthly credits to buy audiobooks they keep, plus access to a catalog of included titles, podcasts, and originals, and they can listen through the app on phones, tablets, and smart speakers. Features such as variable speed, bookmarks, sleep timers, and syncing between listening and reading with Kindle books make it practical for commuting and chores.

Technology is changing how titles are made. Audible has been introducing AI narration for publishers and authors who cannot afford a human narrator, and AI-powered translation and dubbing for audiobooks, alongside AI-based recommendations and summaries. Human narrators remain central to the premium experience, and the shift has prompted debate among narrators and listeners about quality and the future of the profession.

item.title: AutoGrid
item.description:
AutoGrid builds software for the changing electricity grid. As more homes and businesses add solar panels, batteries, and electric vehicles, utilities need ways to coordinate them. AutoGrid’s platform forecasts supply and demand, controls devices, and combines many small resources into virtual power plants that can respond when the grid needs help. Machine learning predicts energy use and optimizes when to charge, discharge, or reduce load.

Utilities and energy retailers use it to run demand response programs, manage commercial and residential batteries, and monetize flexibility in energy markets. It integrates with device makers and energy management systems, so a single platform can orchestrate thermostats, batteries, EV chargers, and industrial loads. The goal is to lower costs and reduce the need for new power plants during peak demand.

item.title: BetterHelp
item.description:
BetterHelp is one of the largest online therapy platforms. You fill out a questionnaire about your needs and preferences, and the service suggests a licensed counselor. You can message your therapist, join live sessions by video, phone, or chat, and schedule at times that suit you, which removes commuting and makes weekly care easier for many people. Therapists are independent licensed professionals such as psychologists, social workers, and counselors.

The pricing model is a recurring subscription based on location and therapist, rather than per-visit billing, and it generally does not accept insurance, which some people find convenient and others find expensive. It is owned by Teladoc Health. Some reviewers praise the convenience and access, while others report difficulty finding a good match or a pushy sales process. Therapy that happens in messages works differently from a weekly hour in an office, and some people prefer live sessions.

item.title: Bloomerang
item.description: Bloomerang is built around donor retention, which is one of the hardest problems in fundraising: many donors give once and never again. The CRM stores each supporter’s contact details, gifts, communications, and notes, and it shows a timeline of every interaction. A generosity score and engagement level help staff see who is likely to give again and who may be slipping away, so they can focus outreach where it counts.

item.title: Bonterra
item.description:
Bonterra was created by combining several nonprofit software companies, including EveryAction, Social Solutions, Network for Good, and CyberGrants. That heritage explains the breadth: the company sells tools for fundraising and donor management, case management for human services programs, volunteer and employee giving programs, grants administration, and online giving pages. Nonprofits can use pieces of it or adopt a larger suite.

The pitch is to connect the work of raising money with the work of delivering programs. A charity can track a donor’s giving next to the services it funds, and a case manager can record outcomes that feed into reports for funders. AI features appear in tasks like drafting fundraising messages, segmenting supporters, and summarizing case notes, with attention to privacy because the data can be sensitive.

item.title: Bugsnag
item.description: Bugsnag tells engineering teams what is breaking in their software and for whom. A small SDK in a web, mobile, or server app reports crashes and handled errors with a stack trace, device and browser details, user information, and the actions that led up to the failure. Instead of a flood of raw events, Bugsnag groups similar errors together, so a single bug appears as one issue with a count of affected users.

item.title: Calm
item.description:
Calm is one of the most downloaded wellness apps. Its content library includes guided meditations of different lengths, sleep stories read by narrators in a soothing voice, calming music, breathing exercises, and masterclasses on topics such as stress and focus. A daily session and reminders encourage a habit. Many people use it mainly to fall asleep, which is where the app is strongest.

The company has extended into other areas. Calm Health offers programs for employers and health plans, with tools for sleep, stress, and mental wellbeing, and content for kids and families. Personalization suggests content based on your goals and mood, and newer features use AI to tailor recommendations. The app is not a substitute for therapy, but it can support relaxation and routines.

item.title: Confluence AI
item.description:
Confluence is where many teams keep their documentation. It organizes pages into spaces, with templates for meeting notes, product requirements, runbooks, project plans, and knowledge bases. Pages support rich formatting, comments, and embedded content from Jira and other tools. Version history and permissions help control who can edit and read what. Teams in engineering, product, IT, and operations use it as a shared source of truth.

AI features come through Atlassian’s Rovo. Inside Confluence, you can summarize a long page, draft content from a short prompt, improve or translate writing, and ask questions in natural language and get answers drawn from the knowledge in your spaces. Rovo search reaches across Confluence, Jira, and connected tools like Google Drive and Slack, and agents can take on tasks such as turning a meeting note into action items.

item.title: Cronometer
item.description:
Cronometer is for people who want to know what is in their food, not only how much of it they eat. You log meals by searching a database, scanning barcodes, or entering recipes, and the app breaks them down into calories, macronutrients, and dozens of micronutrients. Its data comes from verified sources such as government nutrition databases, which makes it more reliable than apps built mostly on user-submitted entries.

Detailed tracking supports use cases like managing a medical diet, checking for vitamin and mineral gaps, tracking fasting or specific eating plans, and training for sports. Targets can be customized, charts show trends, and the app can connect with fitness trackers and devices to account for activity. Newer features use AI to speed up logging, for example by recognizing foods from photos, though human review is wise.

item.title: Dubverse
item.description:
Dubverse helps creators reach audiences who speak other languages. You upload a video or paste a link, and the platform transcribes the speech, translates the script, and generates a dubbed voice track in the target language, timed to match the original. It supports a range of languages, including many Indian ones, and lets you edit the transcript and translation before the voice is produced, which matters for accuracy.

Features support a full localization workflow. You can choose among voices, adjust speed, and edit individual lines, and the platform can add subtitles. An API supports automation for companies that process a lot of content, and a text-to-speech studio produces voiceovers for videos without translation. Typical customers are YouTubers, e-learning teams, news and entertainment publishers, and brands that run content in several markets.

item.title: Embark Veterinary
item.description: Embark’s test starts with a cheek swab at home. You activate the kit, collect a sample from your dog, and mail it to the lab, and results arrive online in a few weeks. The breed report shows a percentage breakdown across hundreds of breeds and how far back each breed appears in the family tree, which owners of mixed-breed dogs often find revealing. It also estimates traits such as coat color and weight.

item.title: Fleetio
item.description:
Fleetio helps organizations that rely on vehicles keep them running. It maintains a record for every vehicle, truck, or piece of equipment, including service history, documents, and costs. Preventive maintenance schedules trigger reminders by mileage, hours, or time, which reduces breakdowns and extends vehicle life. Drivers can complete inspections on a phone app, report issues, and log fuel, and shops can manage work orders and parts.

Data from telematics devices flows into the system, so mileage, location, and diagnostic trouble codes update automatically and can trigger work orders. Reports show total cost of ownership, fuel use, downtime, and compliance items, and integrations connect with accounting, fuel card, and telematics providers. AI features help summarize issues, surface patterns, and suggest actions to reduce cost.

item.title: Geneious
item.description:
Geneious gives molecular biologists a graphical environment for work that would otherwise need command-line tools. Researchers import sequence data from sequencers or databases, then view, align, annotate, and compare it in a visual interface. It supports de novo assembly and mapping of reads to a reference, building phylogenetic trees, designing primers, and planning cloning experiments, so a lab can do many routine tasks in one program.

A plugin system extends it with additional algorithms and workflows, including tools for antibody discovery, metagenomics, and variant analysis. Results are shared through a collaboration feature, and a server product lets teams work with common databases. The software is part of Dotmatics, which also owns other scientific R&D tools. Machine learning appears in specific tools and plugins instead of as a general assistant.

item.title: Grip
item.description:
Grip focuses on a problem every large event has: people attend hoping to meet the right contacts, then wander the floor without finding them. Grip collects attendees’ goals when they register, such as buying a product, finding partners, or recruiting, and uses matchmaking to recommend whom to meet. People can accept suggestions, message one another, and schedule meetings before and during the event.

Organizers get tools to manage the experience. Exhibitors can see qualified leads and capture them at the booth, sponsors get measurable engagement data, and the event team can track how many meetings happened and how satisfied participants were. A mobile app and integrations with registration systems, CRMs, and event platforms connect the pieces. Typical customers are trade show and conference organizers in industries like technology, healthcare, and manufacturing.

item.title: Hinge
item.description:
Hinge takes a different approach from swipe-first dating apps. Profiles are built from photos plus written or voice answers to prompts, which give people something specific to respond to. Users like or comment on a particular part of a profile, which starts a conversation with context.

The app uses algorithms to suggest people likely to be compatible, based on preferences and behavior, and has added AI tools such as prompt feedback to help people write better profiles. It limits how many likes a user can send, which encourages more selective choices, and offers premium tiers.

item.title: Homer
item.description:
Homer is built for young children learning to read and explore. After parents enter a child’s age and interests, the app builds a learning path with activities that include phonics, letter sounds, sight words, stories, math, and creative play, and features content from well-known children’s brands. Lessons are short and playful, with characters and rewards that keep young learners engaged.

Personalization is a selling point: the program adapts to the child’s progress and interests, so a child who loves trains or animals gets content around those themes. Parents get progress reports and ideas for offline activities, and the app is designed to be used with limited screen time. Its approach follows early literacy research, and it has been used in homes and in some schools.

item.title: Hopper
item.description:
Hopper started as a flight price prediction app. It analyzes historical and live fare data to forecast whether a ticket will get cheaper or more expensive, and it tells you to buy now or wait. You can watch a route and get notifications when prices drop, and it highlights flexible dates and nearby airports to save money. The same approach extends to hotels and rental cars.

What sets it apart from simple search tools is a set of financial products around travel. Price Freeze lets you lock a fare for a fee while you decide, and cancellation, change, and delay protections give travelers extra flexibility, usually for an additional cost. Hopper also runs a business that provides these travel and fintech features to other companies through partnerships. Predictions rely on machine learning, but they are estimates, and airline pricing can be unpredictable.

item.title: Jumio
item.description: Jumio helps businesses confirm that a customer is who they claim to be. A user photographs an ID document, such as a passport or driver’s license, and takes a selfie. Jumio checks the document for authenticity, reads the data, compares the selfie to the photo on the ID, and uses liveness detection to make sure a real person is present, not a photo, video, or deepfake. The process takes seconds and replaces in-person checks.

item.title: Kinedu
item.description:
Kinedu helps parents support their child’s early development. After entering a baby’s age, the app creates a plan with short, playful activities for each day, such as tummy time ideas, sensory games, and language exercises, with videos that show how to do them. Activities are grouped by areas like physical, cognitive, social-emotional, and language development.

The app tracks milestones and shows a baby’s progress against typical ranges, explaining what is normal and when to speak to a pediatrician. Articles and guidance from experts cover sleep, feeding, and parenting questions, and parents can keep a journal of moments. Some features use personalization to adjust suggestions to a child’s progress.

item.title: Maxar Technologies
item.description:
Maxar was best known for high-resolution satellite imagery. Its WorldView satellites photographed the Earth in great detail, and governments, news organizations, mapmakers, and businesses used the images for defense and intelligence, disaster response, agriculture, infrastructure monitoring, and navigation. Maxar’s imagery supported mapping products and was often seen in news coverage of conflicts and natural disasters.

Its other major business was space systems: building satellites and spacecraft components for communications, observation, and exploration. Machine learning was applied to extract features such as buildings, roads, and vehicles from imagery at scale, and to create 3D models of the Earth. The company was taken private by a private equity firm and later separated its two main businesses under new names.

item.title: Mermaid Chart
item.description:
Mermaid is a popular open-source way to create diagrams by writing text. You describe a flowchart or sequence diagram in a few lines of code, and it renders as a graphic, which makes diagrams easy to version in Git, embed in documentation, and update alongside code. GitHub, GitLab, and many documentation tools render Mermaid natively, and developers like that diagrams stay in plain text.

Mermaid Chart is the company and product founded by the creator of Mermaid. It provides a web editor with live preview, a visual drag-and-drop editor for people who prefer not to write code, templates, and collaboration features such as sharing and comments. AI can generate diagrams from a description, fix syntax errors, and suggest changes, which lowers the barrier for beginners. Plugins integrate with VS Code, Confluence, Jira, and other tools.

item.title: Meta Quest
item.description:
Meta Quest headsets made virtual reality mainstream by removing the need for cables and a powerful computer. The headsets have built-in processors, controllers, and cameras that track your hands and surroundings, and run apps from the Quest store. The latest models support mixed reality, blending virtual objects with the live view of the room, which opens up games and tools that interact with your space.

The ecosystem includes a wide range of experiences. Popular uses include games, fitness apps, social worlds, watching videos on virtual screens, and creating or collaborating in 3D. Meta is adding AI features, including Meta AI as a voice assistant and tools that help creators build worlds, and headsets can connect to a PC for more demanding games. Models vary in price and capability, and the software is called Horizon OS.

item.title: MyFitnessPal
item.description:
MyFitnessPal is the best-known food diary app. You log what you eat by searching a database of packaged foods, restaurant meals, and homemade recipes, and the app totals calories and macronutrients against daily goals. It syncs with fitness trackers and apps, so exercise adjusts your targets, and it records weight and measurements over time. Millions of people use it for weight loss, muscle gain, or general awareness.

Its size is its strength. The food database is huge, though many entries are user-submitted and can contain errors, so it pays to choose verified items. Features include barcode scanning, recipe import, meal scanning with AI to log from a photo, and voice logging. Premium adds more detailed nutrient tracking, custom goals, macro presets, and meal planning, while a free version covers basic logging.

item.title: NAVEX
item.description:
NAVEX serves compliance and risk teams at large organizations. Its best-known service is a reporting hotline and web portal where employees can raise concerns about misconduct anonymously. Reports flow into a case management system that assigns investigators, tracks actions, and keeps records.

The company also provides policy management, training courses, third-party risk tools, and analytics that reveal patterns across reports. Newer features use AI to summarize cases, categorize reports, and surface trends for compliance leaders.

item.title: New Relic
item.description:
New Relic helps engineering teams understand how their software behaves in production. You add agents or OpenTelemetry instrumentation to your applications and infrastructure, and it collects performance data, errors, logs, and traces of requests as they move through services. Dashboards and alerts show slow endpoints, failing deployments, and resource pressure, and distributed tracing helps pinpoint which service in a chain caused a delay.

The platform covers application performance monitoring, infrastructure monitoring, log management, browser and mobile monitoring, and synthetic checks that test your site from outside. Applied intelligence groups related alerts and reduces noise, and an AI assistant lets people ask questions about their systems in plain language, summarize incidents, and get suggested next steps. It also includes tools for monitoring AI applications, tracking model calls, latency, cost, and quality.

item.title: Noom
item.description:
Noom approaches weight loss as a behavior change problem. After a quiz about your habits and goals, the app builds a plan and delivers short daily lessons based on cognitive behavioral therapy, covering topics like emotional eating, habits, and triggers. A food log uses a color system for food density instead of strict calorie bans, and the app tracks weight, steps, and water.

Support comes through coaching and community. Depending on the plan, users can message a coach, join groups, and use an AI assistant to ask questions and get guidance. Noom has expanded into medical weight management, offering clinician-supervised programs that may include prescription medication in some regions. Programs are meant to help people form sustainable habits.

item.title: Palmetto
item.description:
Palmetto connects homeowners with solar and energy services. A homeowner enters an address and gets an assessment of how much a system could save, compares financing options, and is matched with installers. The company also offers energy management that coordinates devices like batteries and EV chargers.

On the business side, Palmetto provides software and data used by installers, utilities, and fintechs, including tools for sizing systems, tracking incentives, and managing projects. AI helps optimize when to charge or use stored energy based on rates and weather.

item.title: Particle
item.description:
Particle gives hardware teams a full stack for connected devices. It sells development boards and production-ready modules with cellular, Wi-Fi, or Bluetooth connectivity, runs its own device operating system, and provides a cloud console to monitor devices, send commands, and update firmware over the air. Because connectivity, SIM management, and cloud services come bundled, a small team can move from prototype to production without assembling the parts separately.

The platform emphasizes fleet management at scale. Dashboards show device health and data usage, alerts flag problems, and tools support provisioning, remote diagnostics, and secure updates. Webhooks and integrations send data to cloud services and applications, and newer products add more powerful edge computing, including boards that run Android and machine learning workloads at the edge.

item.title: PromptBase
item.description:
PromptBase turned prompts into products. Creators craft prompts that reliably produce a type of result, such as a particular art style, a logo format, or a structured business document, and list them with example outputs. Buyers pay a small amount to get the text, then use it with the relevant AI tool, saving time on trial and error.

The marketplace organizes prompts by model and category, shows sample images, and uses ratings and reviews to help buyers choose. It also supports custom prompt requests and tools for prompt creators to test and sell their work. The business sits on a belief that skilled prompting has value, particularly for image generators where small wording changes make a big difference.

item.title: RapidAPI
item.description:
RapidAPI made discovering APIs easier. Developers browse a catalog of thousands of APIs across categories such as weather, finance, sports, language, and AI, test them in the browser, and subscribe with a single key and billing account. This saves the effort of signing up with every provider separately, and API publishers get a distribution channel and billing.

The company also offered products for businesses, including an enterprise hub for managing internal and partner APIs, and testing tools. Nokia acquired the technology and marketplace to support its efforts to expose telecom network capabilities to developers through APIs, and the public marketplace is expected to continue much as before with some rebranding.

item.title: Ready Player Me
item.description: Ready Player Me offered a way to carry one avatar across many apps. A user took a selfie or built a character in the creator, customized clothing and hair, and received a 3D avatar that worked in a growing network of games, social platforms, and VR worlds. For developers, an SDK and web tools made it easy to add avatars without building a character creator from scratch, and it supported engines such as Unity and Unreal.

item.title: Root Insurance
item.description:
Root built its pitch on the idea that safe drivers should pay less. New customers take a test drive period with the app, which uses the phone’s sensors to measure things such as braking, speed, turning, and time of day driving. Combined with other information, those readings help set the price, so a careful driver can get a lower rate than under traditional pricing based mainly on demographics.

The process is online. People get a quote, buy a policy, and manage their coverage in the app, including proof of insurance and claims. Root also sells through partners, embedding insurance into other companies’ purchasing flows, and has added products such as renters insurance. Machine learning supports pricing, fraud detection, and claims handling.

item.title: Samsara
item.description:
Samsara collects data from the physical world and puts it to work. Gateways and cameras installed on vehicles, trailers, and equipment report location, engine data, driver behavior, and conditions, and the cloud platform presents it through dashboards and apps. Fleet managers use it for tracking, routing, maintenance, compliance with driver hours rules, and safety coaching.

AI dashcams detect risky events like distracted driving, tailgating, and rolling stops, and alert drivers and managers, and video evidence helps with accidents and insurance claims. The platform also covers equipment monitoring, site safety, temperature tracking for cold chains, and workflow tools such as digital forms and inspections. An AI assistant helps users analyze data and set up actions in plain language.

item.title: Schrödinger
item.description:
Schrödinger builds software that simulates molecules. Its approach relies on physics: calculating how atoms interact to predict properties like how strongly a drug candidate binds to a protein. The best-known method, free energy perturbation, estimates binding strength with accuracy useful enough to guide which molecules to make in the lab. Pharmaceutical and biotech companies use the platform to design and screen compounds before synthesizing them.

Machine learning is combined with these simulations. Models trained on simulation results can score vast numbers of molecules rapidly, which makes it possible to explore chemical space far beyond what physical calculations alone could cover. The software suite includes Maestro as the main interface and LiveDesign for collaboration among scientists, with applications in materials science, such as batteries and polymers, alongside life sciences.

item.title: TaxJar
item.description:
TaxJar tackles the complexity of U.S. sales tax for online businesses. Rules differ by state, county, and city, and a seller can owe tax in many places once they pass certain thresholds. TaxJar connects to selling channels such as Shopify, Amazon, WooCommerce, and BigCommerce, pulls in sales data, calculates the tax owed, and shows where the business has obligations. Reports summarize what is due in each jurisdiction.

The service can also file and remit returns in many states for an additional fee, which saves sellers from dealing with each state’s portal. An API provides tax calculations at checkout for platforms and developers. It was acquired by Stripe, which has been building its own tax product, Stripe Tax, and TaxJar continues to operate and support filing, while its role is evolving alongside Stripe’s tools.

item.title: Teladoc Health
item.description:
Teladoc Health delivers healthcare through phones and video. Members can see a clinician for common conditions, get prescriptions where appropriate, and access specialists, therapists, and dermatologists without traveling. Employers and health plans buy the service for their members, which makes access fast and convenient for non-emergency issues, and it includes expert medical opinion services and virtual nursing.

The company also runs programs for chronic conditions, such as diabetes and hypertension, combining connected devices, coaching, and digital tools. Mental health care is a major area, including its consumer therapy brand BetterHelp. AI is used for matching patients with providers, supporting clinicians with documentation, and personalizing care programs.

item.title: Tripadvisor
item.description:
Tripadvisor built its name on traveler reviews. Visitors rate and describe hotels, restaurants, tours, and sights, and the site ranks places based on those opinions, which people use to decide where to stay and eat. Photos, forums, and Q&A add detail. It covers millions of places worldwide and is free to browse.

The site has developed into a booking and planning platform. It compares hotel prices and links to booking partners, sells tours and activities through Viator, and supports restaurant reservations through TheFork. AI trip-planning features create itineraries from a short description, suggest places based on reviews, and organize saved items into trips. Businesses use Tripadvisor to manage their listings, respond to reviews, and advertise.

item.title: TurboTax
item.description: TurboTax makes tax filing a guided interview. You answer plain-language questions, import documents like W-2s and 1099s, and the software fills in the forms, checks for errors, and estimates your refund or amount owed. It supports many situations, from simple returns to investments, self-employment, and rental income, and e-files returns with federal and state tax agencies. It has long been the most recognized brand in consumer tax software in the U.S.

item.title: Uplight
item.description:
Uplight helps utilities communicate with customers and manage demand. It combines data on how households and businesses use energy with tools for personalized messages, home energy reports, smart thermostat programs, and marketplace offers for efficient appliances. The goal is to reduce peak demand and help customers cut bills, which lowers the need for expensive new capacity.

By acquiring AutoGrid, Uplight added software for managing distributed energy resources such as batteries, solar, EV chargers, and flexible loads. Together, the platform can enroll customers, control devices, and optimize their use as a virtual power plant, supported by machine learning for forecasting and targeting. It serves electric and gas utilities in many regions.

item.title: Wanderlog
item.description:
Wanderlog combines a travel notebook with a map. You create a trip, add places such as hotels, restaurants, and attractions, and arrange them by day. The app shows everything on a map with travel times between stops, and can optimize the order to reduce backtracking. It imports reservations from your email, tracks expenses, and works offline on mobile apps, which is handy while traveling.

Collaboration is a main feature. Friends and family can edit the same itinerary at once, vote on places, and share notes and budgets. AI tools suggest destinations and activities, generate draft itineraries from a few preferences, and recommend nearby places based on reviews and guides. A catalog of lists and guides provides inspiration for popular destinations.

item.title: Wingman
item.description:
Wingman positions itself as a coach for dating apps. A user shares their profile or chat, and the AI suggests better photos, rewrites the bio, and proposes replies to messages. The aim is to help people present themselves well and keep conversations going.

AI-written messages raise authenticity questions, since the person on the other end expects to talk to you. Many users prefer feedback and ideas to full ghostwriting. Sharing screenshots of chats involves other people’s messages, so consider privacy.

item.title: Woebot
item.description:
Woebot was one of the best-known mental health chatbots. It talked with users about mood and thoughts, using techniques from cognitive behavioral therapy to help them notice patterns, challenge unhelpful beliefs, and practice coping skills. Conversations were short and structured, with a friendly tone, so people could use it when they felt stressed or anxious, at any time of day.

It differed from general chatbots by using carefully written, clinically reviewed content instead of free-form generation, and the company ran studies to evaluate it. It aimed to make support more accessible and affordable than traditional therapy, and was used by individuals, employers, and health systems. It was always described as a supplement to, not a replacement for, professional care.

item.title: Wysa
item.description: Wysa is a conversational app for stress, low mood, and anxiety. Users chat with a friendly penguin character that asks about how they feel and offers exercises, such as reframing negative thoughts, breathing techniques, sleep tools, and guided meditations. The responses draw on structured therapeutic content written and reviewed by clinicians instead of unconstrained text generation, which is meant to make it safer and more predictable than a general chatbot.

item.title: Zebra Medical Vision
item.description:
Zebra Medical Vision developed AI that reads medical scans and flags findings. Its algorithms examined chest X-rays, CT scans, and mammograms for conditions such as lung nodules, bone density loss, fatty liver, coronary calcium, and signs of fractures, often picking up incidental findings that a radiologist focused on another question might not report. The company had several algorithms cleared by regulators in the United States and Europe.

A distinctive aspect was population health analysis: by screening scans that were already taken for other purposes, hospitals could identify patients at risk of conditions such as osteoporosis or cardiovascular disease and follow up. Zebra Medical Vision offered its tools through a cloud platform that integrated with radiology workflows.

item.title: ContractSafe
item.description:
ContractSafe addresses a basic business problem: contracts scattered across inboxes, shared drives, and filing cabinets. Teams upload agreements into one searchable repository, and the system reads them to pull out key details such as parties, effective dates, renewal terms, and notice periods. Because the text is searchable, finding a specific clause across hundreds of contracts takes seconds instead of hours.

Automation helps avoid missed deadlines. ContractSafe can send alerts before a contract renews or expires, so teams can renegotiate or cancel in time instead of being locked into automatic renewals. Permissions control who can see sensitive agreements, and reports summarize the portfolio by type, value, and upcoming dates. Integrations connect with tools such as Salesforce and Microsoft or Google storage, and an audit trail records activity.

item.title: Workable
item.description:
Workable is an applicant tracking system aimed at small and mid-sized companies. Recruiters create a job, post it to many job boards with one click, and manage candidates through a pipeline with scorecards, notes, and team collaboration. A careers page and templates for emails, offers, and interview kits cover the basics of hiring.

AI features speed up repetitive work. The platform can write job descriptions, suggest candidates from a large database and from your own applicants, screen resumes against criteria, and summarize interview recordings and notes. An AI assistant helps recruiters draft messages and prepare interview questions. Integrations connect to HR systems, calendars, background check providers, and assessment tools.

item.title: Ghostwall
item.description:
Ghostwall belongs to the group of click fraud prevention tools. Advertisers who pay per click can lose money when bots or competitors click ads. The service watches traffic to paid campaigns, looks for suspicious patterns, and blocks the sources that appear fraudulent, for example by adding them to exclusion lists on ad platforms.

Reports show blocked clicks and estimated savings. The ad platforms filter some invalid traffic themselves, so independent tools add value mainly for accounts with significant spend or visible fraud problems. Results depend on how good the detection is, and aggressive blocking can also exclude real customers.

item.title: Ideamap
item.description:
Ideamap lets users start with a topic and watch a map grow. The AI suggests branches, groups related ideas, and links concepts, so brainstorming moves beyond a first list. Users can edit nodes by hand, add notes, and rearrange the canvas.

Typical uses include planning projects, outlining articles, studying a subject, and mapping product ideas. The tool aims to reduce the friction of starting from a blank canvas and help with the organizing step that follows brainstorming.

item.title: MOVA Guide
item.description:
MOVA Guide gives recommendations through conversation. Instead of scrolling through lists of top-rated places, a user tells it something like I want a quiet evening with good food, and it suggests spots matching that mood in their area. It aims to feel more personal than review sites.

The app is aimed at both tourists and residents bored with their usual routine. Suggestions can include restaurants, cafes, activities, and events, and the guide adjusts as the user reacts to ideas.

item.title: PrompTessor
item.description:
PrompTessor gives prompt writers a place to work. Users draft a prompt, get suggestions to improve its structure and clarity, run it against several models, and compare outputs. Analysis tools point out ambiguity and missing context.

Typical users are people who build assistants and automations and need consistent behavior, as well as individuals who want better results from chatbots. Saving and versioning prompts helps teams reuse what works.

Independent information is limited. As models get better at understanding short requests, built-in prompt improvers in chat apps cover some needs. PrompTessor has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include PromptPerfect, PromptLayer, Promptfoo, LangSmith playground, and Anthropic’s prompt tools. PrompTessor suits users who iterate on prompts.

item.title: scalerX
item.description:
ScalerX targets communities and small businesses on Telegram. A user connects a knowledge source, such as documents or a website, configures an agent’s personality and rules, and launches a bot in Telegram that answers questions from that content.

Use cases include customer support, community moderation and FAQs, and onboarding for projects, especially in crypto and creator groups where Telegram is central. No-code setup lowers the barrier.

Independent information is limited, and bots must be tested to avoid wrong answers in public groups. ScalerX has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Botpress, Chatbase, ManyChat, Voiceflow, and Telegram bot frameworks. ScalerX suits community managers deploying Telegram bots.
